title: Step 67-F Step-Up UX, credential self-service and safe action review
description: HIGH-risk Admin frontend security stage. Reconcile existing runtime FIDO credential self-service endpoints into OpenAPI/generated contracts without changing Backend behavior; implement server-mediated Step-Up challenge/verify, short-lived in-memory/server-bound Step-Up review flow, credential list/add/revoke UX with mandatory Step-Up, and a generic safe action-review boundary that never executes later-domain mutations.

dependencies.evidence: PR #356 merged; exact-SHA Canonical CI #1802, Phase A #1301 and CodeQL #947 SUCCESS; terminal Lock release comment 6147507394.

evidence.contract_gap: Credential self-service runtime endpoints are absent from canonical OpenAPI/generated client at the 67-E baseline; Step-Up endpoints are already typed.
evidence.step_up_binding: Backend-issued step_up_token is bound to account + current session and expires in five minutes.
evidence.browser_token_rule: Step-Up token must never be persisted to localStorage/sessionStorage/cookie; use only transient server-mediated review context for the immediate protected action.
evidence.generic_review_boundary: 67-F may review/confirm a safe generic protected action descriptor but must not execute Steps 68-73 domain mutations.
evidence.design_provenance_repair: Canonical CI #1804 failed closed because the intentional credential OpenAPI contract refinement invalidated frozen Step56/57 recovered-source SHA-256 provenance. Repair authority is restricted to the canonical 17-file generator-equivalent hash/manifest cascade; no Product Design screen, state, copy, operation disposition, permission, journey, visual, review status, historical verdict or runtime-release semantics may change.

acceptance_criteria.description: Canonical OpenAPI/generated contract includes the four already-implemented credential self-service endpoints with response/request schemas derived from runtime source; no Backend behavior changes.
Credential list schema exposes only runtime summary fields and never public key, credential_id, sign counter, enrollment secret, session token or other authentication secret material.
Step-Up challenge and verify use typed existing contracts; the returned step_up_token is never persisted in browser storage/cookies or rendered.
Credential self-service is protected by authenticated session; registration and revocation require successful Step-Up immediately before the protected operation.
Registration uses browser WebAuthn create() with runtime challenge options and existing transient serialization. Credential material is not retained after verification.
Revoke review displays only safe credential summary and impact wording; Backend last-credential protection remains authoritative and conflict is handled without optimistic removal.

Generic safe action-review boundary requires explicit user confirmation, captures current authority before Step-Up, never retries mutations blindly, and does not execute later-domain commands in 67-F.
Cancel/expiry/verification failure restores a safe launcher state and discards transient Step-Up/action-review context.
Persian RTL accessibility includes keyboard-safe dialog/review flow, visible focus, safe initial focus, Escape/cancel and launcher focus restoration.
Dashboard runtime and Steps 68-73 domain workspaces remain excluded; no Backend/DB/security-authority mutation is introduced.

HIGH-risk closure requires exact-head Canonical CI, Phase A, CodeQL, independent Security, deterministic Review, exact-artifact ACTIVE Lock, Project Owner Human Gate, protected merge, exact-SHA postmerge verification and terminal Lock release.

Any Step56/57 recovered-source updates caused by the intentional OpenAPI credential contract change are SHA-256 provenance-only across the explicitly authorized 17 files; no Product Design semantics change.

external_gate_evidence.rule: Step 67-F is HIGH risk. Exact-artifact Project Owner approval is mandatory after technical/security/review/Lock evidence is complete.
